WHAT THAT COST AND BOUGHT, measured this session: three modules (~1060 lines) rederived the chi class-invariance, the weighted degree, the drop bounds and the bounded-vanishing assembly. Two findings worth keeping:
  1. The adelic form is sometimes CHEAPER, not just different. chi class-invariance is elementary subspace linear algebra here (multiplication by g maps sections onto shifted sections) and needs NO finiteness and NO chi-additivity, whereas AJCR's sheaf form needs the chi machinery even to state the transport. Look for this asymmetry before assuming a port would have been easier.
  2. The parts that did NOT come across are exactly the ones with machinery behind them: AJCR's base H1 vanishing comes from the FLV-class machine (finite dominant pi : Y -> P1 + fiber divisor), its peel from peel_effective on divisorSheaf. Those became named hypotheses in AJC. So the vanishing lane is assembled but conditional; the degree and drop lanes are unconditional.

ALSO DURABLE: extension-uniformity of a vanishing bound is not merely unproved in AJC, it is not currently STATABLE. All adelic invariants are pinned on a chosen 2-affine cover (deliberately, to avoid the HasCechToHModuleIso gate), and RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean gives C_kappa as an AJC curve but does NOT transport the cover data. Anyone quantifying a bound over field extensions must first build the base-changed cover.

two-cover-Cech-termwise-base-change technique for uniformity -- and note AJCR only ever ran it at
D=0, so even the idea is unproven for general D -- and (b) the finite-pullback degree
multiplicativity strategy for the principal-divisor leaf. Do not promise a mechanical port.
